feature: View to Edit on a long recording, without the hitch
summary: Pressing Cmd-2 on a five minute recording with captions starts the slide into Edit at once. The editor now comes in over a few frames while it slides, so the window never stalls for 190ms before it moves.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Walk: Scripts/playtest/view-to-edit-on-a-long-recording-walk.json.

try.do: Open a long recording (five minutes or more). It opens in View.
Press Captions > Add Captions, or open one that already has captions, then press Cmd-1 to get back to View.
Watch the panel and the tracks as they slide in.
Press Cmd-1, then Cmd-2 again a few times.

evaluate: Does the slide start the moment you press Cmd-2, with no pause before it?
Can you see the panel's sections or the track rows arriving one after another, or does it read as one slide?
Does the View | Edit thumb in the title bar glide smoothly when you press Cmd-2?
rough: The slide itself still draws at a low frame rate going into Edit (each frame takes 30 to 50ms of main thread work), on short recordings too. Edit to View is smooth. Filed as its own task.
The longest single pass is now about 75 to 85ms (it was about 190ms). The heaviest remaining piece is the Captions section's style tiles and dropdowns, built in one pass.
